description_brief: A monstrous guardian of the Cedar Forest appointed by Enlil, whose roar is a whirlwind, flame is in his jaws, and breath is death.
notes: "Appointed by Enlil to safeguard the forest; overcome and killed by Gilgamesh and Enkidu with help from Shamash."

description_brief: A divine bull sent by the god Anu at Ishtar's request, capable of killing hundreds with its fiery breath.
notes: "Sent by Ishtar to punish Gilgamesh; killed by Enkidu and Gilgamesh; Enkidu throws its member at Ishtar."

description_brief: Monstrous guardians, male and female, of the twin mountains of Mashu at the edge of the world, whose glance is death and presence shakes the hills.
symbolism_roles: Threshold Guardians; Boundary Keepers; Awe; Terror
notes: "Guard the passage of the sun; Gilgamesh must pass them to reach Uta-Napishtim."

description_brief: A serpent that steals the plant of rejuvenation from Gilgamesh while he is bathing, frustrating his quest for eternal youth.
Lions hunted by Gilgamesh and Enkidu; also, Gilgamesh wears a lion skin.
notes: Lions are depicted both as ordinary animals to be hunted and as symbols of royalty and wildness  particularly when Gilgamesh wears a lion skin after Enkidu's death.

description_brief: Hunted by Gilgamesh and Enkidu.
notes: Wild asses are associated with Enkidu's wild nature before he is civilized.

description_brief: Released by Uta-Napishtim after the flood.
notes: Used to search for dry land after the flood.  Its return symbolizes the continued presence of floodwaters.

description_brief: Released by Uta-Napishtim after the flood.
symbolism_roles: Messenger, Omens, End of the Flood
notes: The raven's failure to return signifies the receding of the floodwaters and the availability of food on dry land.

description_brief: Loved by Ishtar, who broke its wing.
notes: A brightly colored bird that Ishtar loved but then harmed  leaving it crying "kappi" ("my wing").

description_brief: A serpent that steals the plant of rejuvenation from Gilgamesh while he bathes.
symbolism_roles: Adversary; Thief; Renewal (by shedding skin, contrasted with Gilgamesh's loss); Frustration of human hopes
notes: Snuffs the plant 'Greybeard-who-turneth-to-man-in-his-prime''s fragrance and steals it from Gilgamesh, thus ending his last chance at regaining youth. Often seen symbolically as shedding its skin (renewal) contrasting with Gilgamesh's failure to gain it.

description_brief: Descendant of Cain who attacks Heorot and is killed by Beowulf.
Grendel's mother, who attacks Heorot in vengeance and is slain in her underwater hall.
notes: Her episode mirrors heroic vengeance in monstrous form.

description_brief: Treasure-hoarding fire-drake whose final battle kills Beowulf.
Personified salt sea and monstrous mother defeated by Marduk.
notes: Also represented as a deity in Enuma Elis.

description_brief: Cyclops who traps Odysseus and his men before being blinded by cunning.
notes: Central monster episode of the Odyssey.

description_brief: Multi-headed sea monster who snatches sailors from passing ships.
Devouring whirlpool monster that threatens ships in a narrow passage.
Deadly singers whose knowledge and song lure sailors to destruction.
notes: Odysseus survives by binding himself to the mast.

description_brief: Sleepless dragon guarding the Golden Fleece in Colchis.
notes: Overcome through Medea's drugs and Jason's quest.

description_brief: Tormenting winged beings who foul Phineus' food until driven away by the Argonauts.
Serpentine monster slain by Apollo at Delphi.
Mortal Gorgon whose gaze turns beings to stone and whose head is taken by Perseus.
notes: Her head becomes a weapon and protective sign.

description_brief: Bull-headed monster confined in the Labyrinth of Crete.
notes: A major Theseus-cycle creature in metamorphic tradition.

description_brief: Eight-headed serpent slain by Susanoo, yielding the sword Kusanagi.
notes: Central monster-slaying episode in the Kojiki.

description_brief: Cosmic wolf bound by the gods and destined to break free at Ragnarok.
notes: Child of Loki and major Ragnarok monster.

description_brief: Serpent encircling the world and destined to fight Thor at Ragnarok.
Dragon slain by Sigurd after greed transforms him into a treasure guardian.
notes: Central dragon of the Volsung cycle.

description_brief: Dragon slain by Siegfried before the main action of the Nibelungenlied.
notes: Background source of Siegfried's power and vulnerability.

description_brief: Serpentine enemy of the sun god and force of cosmic disorder.
notes: Appears in Egyptian mortuary and solar mythic imagination.

description_brief: Serpent or dragon who holds back the waters until slain by Indra.
notes: Central adversary in Rig Vedic Indra hymns.

description_brief: Demon king of Lanka whose abduction of Sita drives the Ramayana war.
notes: Also represented as a key figure because he has complex agency.

description_brief: Vanara ally of Rama whose leap to Lanka and devotion are central to the rescue of Sita.
notes: Also represented as a key figure because he is a major character.

description_brief: Great wise bird who raises Zal and later aids his descendants.
notes: A benevolent creature and foster-parent in the Shah Nameh.

description_brief: Powerful demon defeated by Rustem in the Shah Nameh.
Monstrous child of Gaia who challenges Zeus after the Titan succession struggle.
notes: Hesiod presents Typhon as Zeus's last great cosmic adversary.

description_brief: Older generation of divine powers overthrown by Zeus and the Olympians.
notes: Important collective figures in Theogony's genealogy and succession myth.

description_brief: One-eyed giant shepherds who trap and devour travelers.
Many-headed serpent whose heads regrow when cut off.
Fire-breathing lion-goat-serpent hybrid.
Half-man, half-horse beings.
Winged lion with a woman's head who poses riddles.
Invulnerable lion slain by Heracles.
Three-headed hound guarding the entrance to Hades.
Winged horse born from Medusa's blood.
Giant divine bird and mount of Vishnu.
Divine serpent beings associated with water and wisdom.
notes: Vasuki used to churn the ocean.

description_brief: Shapeshifting demons who eat flesh.
Divine monkey warriors who aid Rama.
Serpent or dragon who holds back the cosmic waters.
Dragon who gnaws at the root of Yggdrasil.
Squirrel who carries insults on Yggdrasil.
Eight-legged horse of Odin.
notes: Born when Loki took the form of a mare.

description_brief: One of Odin's ravens who gathers news.
One of Odin's ravens who gathers news.
Blood-stained hound guarding Hel.
Sigurd's horse descended from Sleipnir.
Demon who devours hearts failing judgment.
notes: Has crocodile head, lion front, hippo hind.

description_brief: Solar bird of rebirth associated with Ra.
Mountain goblins mastering martial arts.
Ogres associated with disease and punishment.
Shapeshifting fox spirits.
Forest goblin or demon of the wilderness.
Lake monster of Welsh folklore.
Enchanted wild boar hunted by Arthur.
notes: Central quest of Culhwch and Olwen.

description_brief: The crow form of the Morrigan.
Great wise bird who raises Zal.
Demon defeated by Rostam.
Dragon slain by Siegfried.
notes: Guards treasure. Siegfried bathes in its blood.

description_brief: Dragon in the Volsunga Saga.
